overview: Black strikes with 3...e5 against the Slav, a counter-gambit that gives up the centre for activity. After 4.dxe5 d4 5.Ne4 Qa5+ 6.Bd2 Black plays on the dark squares and White has an extra pawn, or 4.cxd5 cxd5 5.dxe5 d4 leads to similar play. White can play the safe 4.e4 (Anti-Winawer) to avoid theory. Black is tactically active and accepts risk.

white_ideas.idea: Take on e5 and keep the pawn, with Ne4 and Bd2 meeting the checks
Play 4.cxd5 cxd5 5.Nf3 and hold the centre
Develop quickly and return the pawn at the right moment

black_ideas.idea: Push ...d4 to win a tempo on Nc3 and play ...Qa5+
Recapture the e5 pawn with ...Qxe5 or ...Bb4
Use open lines and the queen check for tactics

typical_structures.structure: Black d4 pawn wedge against the white knight
Open centre with White extra pawn on e5

character.notes: A Black counter-gambit with forcing early tactics.

gambit.notes: 4.dxe5 d4 5.Ne4 gives White a pawn that Black can win back only with accurate play; White can keep it.

soundness.notes: Theory considers it unsound but playable for a while; dubious.

structure.notes: Black pawns on d4 and c6 against White's e5: centre opens, open.

approach.notes: A rare gambit, played seldom by strong players.

level.notes: A dubious line, so not for beginners.

sublines_that_differ.name: Anti-Winawer 4.e4
sublines_that_differ.how: White plays e4 immediately and Black gets a different type of position.

level.reason: A dubious gambit is never Beginner.
